title: Delay-induced multistability in one-dimensional swarmalators with common intrinsic frequency
authors: Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, Timoteo Carletti, Kevin P. O'Keeffe
abstract: We study the delayed one-dimensional swarmalator model when all units share a common intrinsic frequency ω. Unlike the zero-frequency case, ω cannot be removed by a rotating-frame transformation because delayed interactions retain the phase accumulated over the lag. The result is a two-order-parameter analogue of the delayed Kuramoto model: the asynchronous state acquires incoherence lobes, the synchronized state becomes a rotating branch stable even when both the spatial and phase couplings are repulsive, and the phase wave develops narrow resonant stability bands. These delay-selected windows overlap to produce broad branch coexistence, including a narrow window near K=-J where all three canonical states-asynchronous, phase wave, and synchronized-are simultaneously stable. In regions where no canonical branch is stable, the order parameters oscillate persistently.
summary: This work analyzes a delayed 1D swarmalator model with a common intrinsic frequency, revealing that the system can host three distinct, simultaneously stable dynamical states. The key finding is the existence of a narrow parameter window where asynchronous, synchronized, and phase wave states coexist. This demonstrates how delay and non-zero intrinsic frequencies can induce complex, non-trivial multistability in non-equilibrium many-body systems.
main_problem: The study investigates delay-induced multistability in a one-dimensional swarmalator model when all interacting units share a common non-zero intrinsic frequency.
main_result: The system exhibits a striking triple coexistence of three distinct stable states—asynchronous, synchronized, and phase wave—in a narrow parameter window, a phenomenon enabled by the non-zero common frequency and delay.
method: The analysis combines stability theory (linearization, Fourier mode analysis) with numerical simulations, including direct perturbation-norm checks, to map out complex parameter regimes.
model_or_system: The model is a delayed one-dimensional swarmalator on a ring, described by coupled equations of motion involving spatial and phase couplings ($K$ and $J$) and a time delay ($	au$).
key_observables: Order parameters ($r, s$), stability boundaries in the $(K, 	au)$ plane, and the persistence/decay rates of perturbations ($\Delta f$).
important_parameters: Common intrinsic frequency ($\omega$), coupling constants ($K, J$), and time delay ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on linear stability theory and perturbation methods, although the authors note that quasiperiodic or transient dynamics cannot be entirely excluded.
figures_summary: Figure 3 maps the stability regions showing the coexistence of the three canonical states; other figures illustrate power spectra and stability dependence on $\omega$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the stability of three canonical states (asynchronous, synchronized, phase wave) under a common frequency $\omega$, culminating in the demonstration and characterization of the triple coexistence region.
why_interesting: The emergence of complex, delay-induced multistability in a classical, non-equilibrium system provides a rich analogy for understanding pattern formation and multiple stable phases in open quantum systems or driven many-body dynamics.

Right: Welch power spectra of r and s, showing sharp peaks at a domi- nant frequency and its harmonics (period ≈30) rather than broadband noise.
